q: A halogen atom attached directly to a benzene ring carbon gives
why: Halogen bonded directly to an aromatic ring carbon defines an aryl halide.

q: The best laboratory method to convert an alcohol into the corresponding chloride, giving a pure product, uses
why: SOCl2 gives R-Cl with by-products SO2 and HCl escaping as gases, leaving a pure product.

q: The Finkelstein reaction converts an alkyl chloride/bromide into an alkyl iodide using
why: NaI in dry acetone displaces Cl/Br since NaI is soluble but NaCl/NaBr precipitate, driving the reaction forward.

q: SN2 reactions proceed with which stereochemical outcome?
why: The nucleophile attacks from the back side opposite the leaving group, inverting the configuration.

q: The rate law for an SN1 reaction is
why: SN1 is unimolecular; the rate-determining step is carbocation formation, depending only on substrate concentration.

q: Dehydrohalogenation of 2-bromobutane with alcoholic KOH gives mainly but-2-ene rather than but-1-ene because of
o: Saytzeff's rule (more substituted alkene is major)
why: Saytzeff's rule states the more stable, more substituted alkene forms as the major elimination product.

q: Among R-Cl, R-Br and R-I, which reacts fastest with magnesium metal to form a Grignard reagent?
why: C-I bond is weakest, so alkyl iodides react fastest with Mg: reactivity order R-I > R-Br > R-Cl.

q: A Grignard reagent reacting with formaldehyde (HCHO) followed by hydrolysis gives
why: HCHO has no alkyl substituent, so addition of RMgX followed by hydrolysis yields a primary alcohol.

q: Freons (CFCs), once used as refrigerants, are now phased out mainly because they
why: CFCs release chlorine radicals in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone molecules.

q: Which compound was historically used as an anaesthetic and is now mainly used as an industrial solvent?
why: Chloroform was once used as an anaesthetic in surgery and is now used mainly as a solvent.
